messages.author: 9a5b747b943f32d3
messages.subject: Some questions related to inla.merge()
parts:
Hi INLA team,


I have three small questions about the inla.merge() function. For simplicity, say I have a set of competing models with the same formula but each having a different graph (e.g., y ~ f(id, model = 'bym2', graph = W_{model})).


inla.merge offers a super easy way to merge models with the same formula and a set of hyperparameters that are fixed to different values.


  • Do graphs count as hyperparameters? From the function/verbose, it seems ok to merge all my models with the function and then work with the merged marginals but I'd like to double-check that it's fine?


  • I am looking for a way to do a posterior predictive check with the inla.merge object. Is it ok to use an inla.merge object with inla.posterior.sample? 


  • To which extent should the formula be 'the same' ? For example, if some models are y ~ x + f(id, model = 'bym2', graph = W_{model}) and others are y ~ x + f(id, model = 'besag2', graph = W_{model}) and that I want to focus on predictors (and not on each parameter) and related quantities is that fine to use inla.merge? Could inla.posterior.sample be used in this case?


Best,

Olivier

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Some questions related to inla.merge()
parts:
good question. the documentation should be more clear on this point, I
see. I'll fix that.

the formula and all lengths, should be the same. possible applications,
include like fixing a parameter to a set of values with various weights,
and then we use inla.merge() to integrate that one out. this is useful
where a model is a _conditional_ Latent Gaussian model.

you cannot sample from the merged object, but you can always sample from
a mixture of inla-models. just sample from a multinomial scaled by the
total number of samples where the probabilities is from the marginal
likelihood or others. then sample for each model and then combine.

as said, I'll make the doc more clear.

Best
H
